body: The core issue here is that if a toolchain isn't registered, toolchain resolution's exception doesn't validate in SkyframeBuildView.assertSaneAnalysisError, and a crash happens instead of just reporting the error.
@excavador Can you help me reproduce this by telling me exactly what git repo you have cloned, and what commands you are running?

Give me some time, I will prepare minimal repo for reproduce.
It also another bug there 
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go/issues/943

Interesting. I can not reproduce problem in clean repo.

Trying to find dependency combination for reproduce the problem

There is a test specifically for this error:
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/35371a88c27f620e09537fe82fd8263396949fe7/src/test/shell/bazel/toolchain_test.sh#L183

so I was surprised to see it. It must be a very specific setup to cause this. I will keep looking at the code but I can't see a code path where this would be caused.

I have the repo with the problem
https://github.com/excavador/bazel_vendor_bug
@katre please get second commit, I updated README.md
Okay, I can only reproduce this on a Mac, which is pretty interesting to start with. Debugging now.

Keep me informed! :)

I little surprised, because I just tried switch our make-based build system to bazel (before this I two months time-to-time learn bazel & skylark).

Pretty interesting fact, the problem reproduced only on full vendor directory with current versions.
If try to create repo with latest dependencies versions, particullary latest openzipkin-go, no problem then.
So, this problem does not block me, but definitely we have some problems in bazel and rules_go, and this case is good point to improve their :)

Looks like the problem is specifically with the case where a rule asks for more than one toolchain, and one of them is missing.

Occurs here:
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go/blob/ad076c97335c03319280fa438c9f958e7c81597a/proto/def.bzl#L56

Note: I don't think the go rules are wrong, I think Bazel is wrong.
And the reason it only expresses as an error on Macs is because of non-determinism in how Skyframe handles getValues() calls
I have a fix, trying to write a test now.
